issue.title: heap-buffer-overflow in _io__RawIOBase_read

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump
pre-release feature fixes, bugs and security fixes

issue.body:
# Crash report

### What happened?

```python
import io
import unittest
class CTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    pass
class BufferedReaderTest:
    read_mode = 'rb'
class MockRaw(io.RawIOBase):
    def __init__(self, data=r'\n\r\t'):
        self._buf = memoryview(data)
        self._pos = 0
    def readable(self):
        return True
    def readinto(self, b):
        if self._pos >= len(self._buf):
            return 2147483647
        n = min(len(b), len(self._buf) - self._pos)
        self._pos += n
        return n
class CBufferedReaderTest(BufferedReaderTest, CTestCase):
    tp = io.BufferedReader
    def test_initialization(self):
        rawio = MockRaw(b'abc')
        bufio = self.tp(rawio)
        self.assertEqual(bufio.read(), b'abc')
if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

comments.body:
More minimal reproducer: 

```python3
import io

class MockRaw(io.RawIOBase):
    def readinto(self, b):
        return 2147483647

MockRaw().read()
```

The generic "read" implementation in `iobase.c` currently assumes `.readinto()` will return a value between "0" and the length of the buffer; but it can return any value. I think a range check should be added (working on a patch):

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/421a475c87771d46752c27def264e5c622a58427/Modules/_io/iobase.c#L936-L949
